deviations.text: Candidate selection, which production runs inside its database, is reimplemented over a local copy of the index. Its settings are copied from the production code at the recorded commit, and the run refuses to start if any copied setting differs from that code. Turning search hits into the set of relevant repositories uses the production function itself.

The code index is built offline by the production chunker and the production embedding call at each repository's pinned commit, and searched by an exact in-memory similarity scan instead of the production database. Similarity values can differ from the database's in their last decimal places.
The source text the ranking stages read for each candidate comes from the offline index at the pinned commit. Production re-fetches the same lines from the code host at the indexed commit.

There is no help-desk ticket. The issue title and body (the protocol's input rule) are given to the production language detection and extraction calls as a ticket body with no source-provider label, no conversation thread and no attachments, and the workspace extraction language is the production default.

Each case is mapped as if it were the only open issue in the workspace. Production first compares a new ticket with issues already in the workspace and can attach it to an existing one instead of mapping it again; that comparison does not run here.
Nothing is written to a database. Usage, reasoning and the second ranking stage's and the repository-search stage's bookkeeping writes are discarded; none of them feeds the stored order.

Production runs the mapping as a sequence of job-runner steps; the harness calls the same production functions in the same order in one process, and refuses to start if the production mapping function calls them differently. Production retries a failed step through its job runner; the harness repeats the same call in process, up to the same number of attempts. A ranking call that still returns no usable answer is scored as a case with no mapping, because production would store none. A provider or network failure is retried on a later resume instead of being scored, in the second ranking stage and in the repository-search stage alike; after three attempts the order production keeps when that stage has no answer is scored.

The production commit and the deployed settings of the second ranking stage and of the repository-search stage are declared by the operator for the run and checked against the code at that commit, not read from the running production system.

The repository-search stage reads the files from the local clone at the pin instead of the code host's archive. The files are the pinned commit's own contents, read from the clone's object store in the order the archive lists them, with the sizes the archive declares; files the repository's export rules keep out of an archive are left out, and which of the rest the stage holds is decided by the production rule itself.

Production reads each repository's settings from its database. The harness describes each repository to the repository-search stage by its name and pinned commit only; the settings it leaves out name the link stored beside a location the stage adds, which is not scored.
